Somatic missense mutations in the N-terminal FERM domain of JAK3 were found in adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma patients and induced gain of function in JAK3; these mutant JAK3s were inhibited by a specific kinase inhibitor.

payload.statement: R103H is a buried-core substitution in the JAK3 FERM domain. Replacing arginine with histidine removes a side-chain interaction that holds the FERM fold together, so the protein is destabilised or misfolded and degraded, which lowers JAK3 levels and signalling.
payload.would_refute: An AlphaFold model or experimental model shows R103 side chain solvent-exposed (relative SASA above about 25%) with no polar or salt-bridge partner, and a stability predictor (e.g. FoldX or Rosetta ddG) gives |ddG| below 1 kcal/mol for R103H.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: Ranked first because the starting evidence on this residue is all indirect but points one way: high conservation (E14 0.898), strongly deleterious predictors (E12 AlphaMissense 0.84, E15 popEVE -3.8, E16 EVE 0.83), a FERM-domain location (E4, E7), and a recessive LOF SCID phenotype (E1, E10). Rank 1 is not strong: G2 and G3 say the residue's structural environment and effect on stability are unknown, and no assay covers R103 (G1, G5). The substitution-specific evidence in E2 (R103C also pathogenic) supports that the residue itself matters, not which mechanism. Missing: per-residue burial or ddG calculation on the AlphaFold model, and any expression or stability data.

payload.statement: R103H folds normally but removes a surface contact that JAK3 needs to couple to the common gamma chain (IL2RG) or other cytokine receptors through its N-terminal FERM region, so receptor association and STAT activation fail.
payload.would_refute: In a predicted JAK3 complex with the gamma chain or a cytokine receptor intracellular region (e.g. AlphaFold-Multimer or a docking model), R103 lies more than 10 Å from any receptor residue, and its buried surface area does not change between wild type and R103H.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: Ranked second because the record ties the FERM N-terminus to receptor binding (E5, a UniProt region annotated for cytokine receptor interaction, though based on sequence similarity) and lists known partners (E20), and E10 shows JAK3 loss of function causes SCID. Still weaker than the folding hypothesis: E5 is inferred by similarity, no retrieved source places residue 103 at a receptor contact (G2, G3), and the gamma-chain association point is unverified. Missing: a receptor-complex model and any co-immunoprecipitation data for R103H.

payload.statement: R103H sits at an intramolecular FERM-SH2 or FERM-kinase interface. Losing the arginine breaks the autoinhibitory or scaffold contact that positions the kinase domain, so catalytic output is reduced.
payload.would_refute: In the AlphaFold model, R103 has no atom within 5 Å of any SH2 or kinase-domain residue, and the FERM-SH2 and FERM-kinase interface contacts are unchanged when R103H is modelled, so the residue sits outside the inter-domain interface.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: Ranked third because its only support is an analogy: E8 is a crystal structure of the Jak2 FERM-SH2 module, not JAK3, and the interface location of R103 is unverified (G2). E11 is about gain of function from ATP binding, not loss of function, so it does not favour this mechanism. Missing: JAK3 domain-boundary mapping of residue 103 and a comparison of R103 with the Jak2 interface residues after alignment.

payload.uncertainty: T1 is one FoldX run on a single AlphaFold model. FoldX errors on predicted models are near 1 kcal/mol, so the +4.15 value is large enough to be informative but is still a prediction. A destabilising ddG does not show that the protein is actually misfolded or degraded in cells, or that the loss of signalling comes from stability rather than from a surface or interface defect. The within-site control is R103C at +2.02 kcal/mol, which is also destabilising and consistent with a site-level stability effect. It does not separate H1 from H2 or H3, since loss of a surface or interface contact could also appear as a stability change in the model. Still needed: relative SASA and side-chain partners of R103 (the direct H1 refute check), the interface readout (T2) for H2 and H3, and ideally an experimental stability or expression assay on R103H.

payload.text:
## Question
What molecular mechanism best explains the loss of function of JAK3 p.Arg103His (P52333), and can one targeted computational test check it? [E1]

## Evidence
ClinVar lists the variant as Pathogenic, with multiple submitters and no conflicts [E1]. Residue 103 lies in the annotated FERM domain, residues 24-356 [E4, E7]. No experimental structure in the Protein Data Bank observes residue 103 [E17, G4]. No retrieved paper reports R103H, or any change at residue 103, in a functional or structural assay [G1]. The AlphaFold model AF-P52333-F1 covers the full sequence, mean pLDDT 85.69 [E18]. AlphaMissense and EVE score the variant as likely pathogenic; these are computational predictions only [E12, E16].

## Agent-generated hypotheses
- H1 (stability/folding, agent-generated hypothesis): R103H is a buried-core substitution that destabilises the FERM fold [H1]. Favoured before the test, starting rank 1.
- H2 (protein interaction, agent-generated hypothesis): R103H removes a surface contact needed for gamma-chain or cytokine-receptor coupling [H2].
- H3 (domain interface, agent-generated hypothesis): R103H breaks a FERM-SH2 or FERM-kinase contact [H3].

## Tests considered and the choice
T1 (stability_effect) was chosen: it had the best learning-to-cost score, needed no compute seconds and no approval, and safety cleared it [T1]. T2 (structural_context) was kept as a follow-up because its interface readout is not covered for this residue [T2]. T3 (structure_comparison) was rejected because the provider was down and it needed approval and 120 compute seconds [T3].

## Result
FoldX predicts a ΔΔG of +4.15 kcal/mol for R103H on AF-P52333-F1, above the 2.0 kcal/mol destabilising threshold, at a local pLDDT of 95.88 [T1, E21]. R103C at the same residue gives +2.02 kcal/mol [E22].

## Updated decision
H1 was favoured before the test and remains favoured after it, so the decision did not change [H1]. H1 is supported; H2 and H3 are unchanged because T1 does not measure their contacts [H2, H3]. No reopening was needed.

## Uncertainty and validation still needed
This is one FoldX run on one predicted model, so it is a computational prediction, not an experimental measurement. It does not show that R103H is misfolded or degraded in cells. Relative solvent exposure and side-chain partners of R103 were not measured, so H1's refute check has not been run. H2 and H3 remain untested. No experimental validation has been done.

## Next experiment
Compute relative SASA and side-chain partners of R103 on AF-P52333-F1, together with the T2 pocket and interface readout [H1, T2]. H1 is refuted if SASA is above 25% with no polar partner. An experimental stability or expression assay on R103H would be the validation step.
